headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared document workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge, but both agents can ingest and transmit content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io diagrams and uses MCP plus browser-based AI-assisted visualization; superset can consume upstream outputs through its Superset API and networked workflows. A shared file or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled document content steer B's downstream interpretation. No direct pairwise bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files, MCP messages, or copied text without provenance checks, prompt injection is plausible.
IF B treats A-generated document text as instructions, malicious content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported document text.
Add a provenance tag to A outputs before B reads them.
Require B to treat A outputs as untrusted data only.
Use a manual review step for any A-generated content before B acts on it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, while B has allowlisted egress and may receive shared workspace content through the pairwise workflow. If sensitive PDFs or text files processed by A are forwarded into B, leakage can occur in default document-processing setups. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A processes documents containing secrets or personal data and forwards them to B, leakage risk exists.
IF both agents share a workspace or copied outputs, B may receive data A touched.
mitigations: Strip secrets from inputs before A processes them.
Restrict B to allowlisted destinations only.
Separate workspaces for A and B.
Turn off automatic forwarding of A outputs into B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and broad network egress; B has allowlisted egress and a Superset API, but neither profile shows shared filesystem writes, git mutation, or overlapping mutable scopes. A conflict pathway is possible only if an external orchestrator gives both write access to the same resource, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts can occur.
IF both are pointed at the same Superset objects or shared files, last-writer-wins errors are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate write targets to each agent.
Use locking or single-writer orchestration.
Keep A and B on separate projects or datasets.
Review any shared mutable resource before enabling concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and B exposes a Superset API for analytics workflows. If B consumes A's extracted facts or diagram interpretations without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. The profiles do not show explicit automation, so medium fits the documented inference chain.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated summaries or extracted facts without validation, errors can propagate.
IF A's diagram or PDF interpretation is used as authoritative input to B, downstream outputs may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source-document checks before B uses A outputs.
Add a human approval step for A-to-B handoffs.
Keep raw source files attached to any B-side derived output.
Flag low-confidence extractions from A for review.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles API keys and document content, while B's profile shows no touched data classes or special compliance constraints. There is no documented residency, retention, or certification mismatch between them, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. Because B's compliance posture is underspecified, the risk remains low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A and then exported into B, compliance review is needed.
IF retention or residency policies differ in the surrounding deployment, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify inputs before sending them to A or B.
Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workflow.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Review residency and DPA requirements before deployment.
